seoContent.title: Free online ASCII toolkit
seoContent.intro: ASCII Tools brings together four online generators to turn your ideas into copy-paste-ready ASCII art: file trees, tables, mini-charts (sparklines) and text banners. Everything runs right in your browser, with no signup or install, and the output fits anywhere: READMEs, technical docs, code comments, the terminal or messages.

whyUse.title: Why use ASCII tools?
whyUse.para1: ASCII text is universal: it looks the same everywhere, without relying on images or complex formatting. Whether you're documenting a project, preparing a README or illustrating a terminal, these tools offer several benefits:
whyUse.benefit1: Universal compatibility: renders correctly on GitHub, GitLab, in the terminal and in every text editor
whyUse.benefit2: Instant integration: paste the result into Markdown, code or an email with no extra formatting
whyUse.benefit3: Version-friendly: changes stay readable and easy to track in your Git commits
whyUse.benefit4: Lightweight and fast: plain text, no heavy images or external dependencies

howToUse.title: How does it work?
howToUse.para1: Every tool follows the same simple flow, from picking the tool to the final copy-paste:
howToUse.step1: Pick the right tool: file tree, table, ASCII chart or text banner
howToUse.step2: Enter your data: file structure, table values, number series or text to style
howToUse.step3: Customize the output with the options: style, sorting, alignment, character format
howToUse.step4: Copy the generated ASCII and paste it into your README, documentation or terminal
howToUse.para2: Everything is computed in real time in your browser: no data is sent to a server, and the output refreshes instantly with every change.

useCases.title: Use cases
useCases.para1: ASCII tools are handy in many everyday situations for developers and technical writers:
useCases.useCase1: Document a web project's structure (React, Next.js, Vue.js…) with a clear file tree
useCases.useCase2: Present comparative data in an aligned ASCII table, right inside a README
useCases.useCase3: Summarize trends (sales, traffic, performance) with compact sparklines in your reports
useCases.useCase4: Create stylized text banners for script headers, logs or terminal welcome messages
useCases.para2: Whether you're on Windows, macOS or Linux, these online tools work on every operating system, with no installation required.

features.title: The available tools
features.para1: ASCII Tools gathers four complementary generators, all free and signup-free:
features.feature1: ASCII Tree: build file and folder trees by drag & drop, perfect for your READMEs
features.feature2: ASCII Table: turn your data into aligned tables, ready to paste into code or Markdown
features.feature3: ASCII Charts: visualize number series as compact mini-charts (sparklines)
features.feature4: Text Banners: convert text into large stylized ASCII banners
features.feature5: Real-time preview and one-click export (copy or download)
features.feature6: Multilingual interface available in 8 languages, with light and dark mode
features.para2: All of these tools are available for free, without signup and directly in your web browser.
